schema_note: PROJECT TRACKING / ORCHESTRATION CORRECTION ONLY. Corrects the Ride project milestone/critical-path model so it matches already-Locked Phase-3 authority and removes the artificial operational dependency cycle currently encoded in the prior M3/M4 project-tracking entries. Does NOT change Chapter-12 Approval semantics, Chapter-13 Quality-Gate semantics, waive any Feature Engine Quality-Gate finding, implement any downstream module, or grant any approval.
central_correction: There is no authoritative standalone 'Feature Engine Module Approval Gate' under current Chapter 12 / Chapter 13. Feature Engine's remaining Quality-Gate evidence (M2) may remain BLOCKED while bounded Phase-3 development continues downstream according to Chapter 14 §14.2.

boundary.note: docs/constitution/12-approval-gates.md fresh-read for content (no blob pinned by the task); its own §12.2/§12.3 content is quoted verbatim below.

authority_finding_1_no_feature_engine_mo.chapter_12_section_12_2: Defines only a 'Phase Approval Gate — prerequisite aggregation' at the Product Owner PHASE decision boundary. Quality gates are one of eight eligibility prerequisite items (item 5: 'applicable quality gates ... đã pass'), never a standalone module-level gate. Section explicitly states it does not redefine internal rules owned by other chapters (§12.3 authority map).
authority_finding_1_no_feature_engine_mo.chapter_13_section_13_1: Explicit: 'Quality Gate pass ≠ Product Owner approval'; 'Quality Gate fail ≠ Product Owner rejection'; 'Quality Gate → sinh eligibility evidence'; 'Approval Gate → consume evidence đó (Chapter 12 §12.2(5))'. Quality Gate 'không approve, không lock, không quyết định phase transition' — it only supplies evidence to Chapter 12; Product Owner remains the sole decision authority.
authority_finding_1_no_feature_engine_mo.phase_3_rules_section_11_gate_path_model: docs/governance/phases/phase-3-rules.md §11 ('Gate-path controls') confirms the expected sequence to Phase 3's Approval Gate: 'Phase 3 module/artifact implementation -> Quality Gate theo Tier cho từng module/artifact -> Phase-wide Backward Consistency Check -> Phase-level Gate review(s) -> Product Owner Phase 3 Approval Gate decision' — a SINGLE phase-level Approval Gate at the end, not a per-module gate inserted between each adjacent Chapter-14 node. Quality Gate evidence accumulates per-module/artifact without itself gating downstream implementation.

other_authorities_checked.lean_ride_operating_model_v1_candidate: No 'module approval' or 'module-level approval' concept found.
other_authorities_checked.module_registry_yaml: No module-approval-gate declaration found; entries carry only 'status: candidate' lifecycle markers, unrelated to Approval Gate semantics.
other_authorities_checked.adr_045: Delegated Technical Resolution model; does not define a module approval gate — only routes decisions between DTR-eligible and Product-Owner-reserved categories.

authority_finding_1_no_feature_engine_mo.generic_reservation_phrase_found: docs/constitution/00-governance.md's Product Owner Decision route listing includes 'Phase/Module Approval Gate decisions' as a reserved-decision CATEGORY (i.e., IF a governing authority ever defines a Module Approval Gate, that decision would be Product-Owner-reserved, non-delegatable) — this is a reservation rule, not a process definition. It does not itself create, define, or imply the existence of a standalone Feature Engine Module Approval Gate.
authority_finding_1_no_feature_engine_mo.conclusion: No controlling authority (Chapter 12, Chapter 13, Phase-3 Rules, Lean Ride Operating Model, module-registry.yaml, ADR-045) defines a separate, standalone Feature Engine (or any single-module) Approval Gate. The prior milestone.md M3 entry ('Feature Engine — Module Approval', citing Chapter 12 §12.2) was a project-tracking / orchestration modeling error, not backed by the cited authority.
authority_finding_1_no_feature_engine_mo.explicit_non_claim: This finding is NOT permission to waive Feature Engine Quality Gates. Quality-Gate evidence requirements (EVID-04/EVID-06/EVID-08) are entirely unaffected and unchanged.

authority_finding_2_downstream_developme.chapter_14_section_14_2_sequence: Data Layer -> Structure Engine & Raw Regime Engine (song song, doc lap) -> Feature Engine -> Context Projection -> Strategy -> Decision -> Risk Gateway -> Execution
authority_finding_2_downstream_developme.phase_3_rules_requirement: Phase-3 Rules §1 quotes this sequence verbatim (no redefinition authority) and §8 (anti-pattern list, item 8) requires: 'mọi transaction Phase 3 PHẢI verify trực tiếp dependency state (đúng G-VERIFY-001) trước khi author một module ngoài thứ tự' — i.e., verify DEPENDENCY STATE (upstream module's own executable/contract boundary), not upstream module's own Quality-Gate PASS status, before authoring a module out of order.
authority_finding_2_downstream_developme.no_mandatory_per_module_approval_gate: Confirmed via §11's own gate-path model (see authority_finding_1) — Quality Gate evidence accumulates per-module without a Product Owner Approval Gate required between each adjacent Chapter-14 node.
authority_finding_2_downstream_developme.conclusion: Feature Engine M2 may remain externally BLOCKED while the primary implementation critical path advances to the next legitimate Chapter-14 node (Context Projection), because dependency-STATE verification (executable/contract boundary), not Quality-Gate PASS, is what Phase-3 Rules actually require before authoring the next module.
